pages.title: The band’s arrangement board
pages.caption: Imagine a band planning a song. They could argue their options in a long group chat, where decisions get buried, or they could use a shared arrangement board to keep everything visible and organized. A canvas is the app’s arrangement board for human-agent work.

pages.title: A shared control panel
pages.caption: A canvas is bidirectional: you and the agent can both change the same board. GitHub Copilot adds plan steps to the board. You uncheck a step, or write "pause before edits" in the notes. GitHub Copilot continues from your update, not from a buried chat sentence.

pages.title: The exercises’ terms
pages.caption: An agent-callable action is an action that the canvas gives the agent, such as updating a checklist item. User scope means the canvas is available to you across projects and is not committed to this repository. Local-only UI is a control that changes only what you see. An event is a recorded state change. Polling checks at intervals for a state change. A timeout is the longest an action can run before it stops.

pages.title: Built-in surfaces come first
pages.caption: The **Plan**, **Terminal**, **Browser**, and **Changes** panels that you used in earlier chapters come with every session. A canvas adds one more surface that you design for the task.

pages.title: Chat, or a canvas?
pages.caption: Use chat for a quick answer to a short task. Use a canvas when the work has state to keep visible, steps that repeat, or controls that you and the agent both use.

pages.title: Make ready
pages.caption: Use **Create from** > **Branches** > `main` to start a new worktree session for the course repository. Select **Interactive** mode and, if an agent picker appears, **Default agent**. In the review panel’s **Terminal** tab, from `samples/book-app-web`, run `npm install`, `npm test -- --run`, and `npm run build`. All three should finish without errors. Note the test totals: your canvas will use them as its baseline.

pages.title: Try a community canvas
pages.caption: Awesome GitHub Copilot is a curated collection of agents, instructions, skills, and canvas extensions. Its Repository Issues Kanban pulls repository issues into a board that you can triage and track inside a session. Select **Open in Copilot app**, confirm the name `accessibility-kanban@awesome-copilot`, and select **Install**. Submit the prompt `Restart canvas extensions`, then select **+** (**Add tab**), **Canvas**, and **Repository Issues Kanban**. Move only one card to **Plan**: each one starts a new agent run.

pages.title: A Session Board
pages.caption: Type `/` in the prompt box and select `/create-canvas`, then describe the board: a Feature proposal text field, a checklist with Plan, Implement, and Validate, and a Notes section with Next decision and Blocker fields. You and the agent can both read and update them. The board does not run tests or edit the app, and **Changes** lists no changed files.

pages.title: The Feature Workbench
pages.caption: A reusable canvas that manages the local development inner loop for a new book-app feature. It keeps the feature proposal, plan, implementation, and evidence linked to the same session. Five stages: **Propose**, **Plan**, **Baseline**, **Implement**, and **Validate**. One feature proposal field and one **Generate plan** button. Eight checklist items. Actions for baseline, implementation, browser validation, final checks, and evidence refresh. An empty evidence area before any action runs.

pages.title: What the prompt asks for
pages.caption: "Every button = agent-callable action": each button asks the agent to do real work, not just change your screen. Plan approval happens only in the session’s **Plan** tab, not through a canvas popup. The canvas checks the plan’s approval status periodically. Test, build, and browser actions get a multi-minute timeout. "Never block on tooling": if the agent cannot save a screenshot or run a browser check, it records a note and the workflow continues. "User scope": the canvas is saved to your machine across projects.

pages.title: Repair, don’t regenerate
pages.caption: Generated results can differ between runs. Check the expected structure before you continue, and do not repeatedly regenerate the full canvas. If one part is wrong, use the repair prompt that matches: parts are missing; items show as complete without evidence; actions stop before the work finishes; an action stays disabled; an action shows an error after its work is done. If the canvas still does not match after two focused repairs, use the Markdown fallback.

pages.title: Run the workbench
pages.caption: Paste the proposal and select **Generate plan**. Review the plan in the **Plan** tab, then select **Exit plan mode and I will prompt myself**, not **Approve and implement this plan**. Select **Run baseline** and compare its totals with the tool output. Select **Implement**, then check the **Changes** pill. Select **Browser validation**, then check the states yourself and stop the dev server. Select **Run final checks**: the tests and the build pass, and the final test total is at least the baseline total.

pages.title: What Inkwell’s mapmakers know
pages.caption: A canvas gives the session a visible, shared board in the side panel. Create that board with `/create-canvas` and a short description. Community canvases from Awesome GitHub Copilot let you install and try the interaction model before building your own. Evidence on the board should come from actual terminal or browser output, not from chat inference.

pages.title: Your turn: an Assess stage
pages.caption: Extend the Feature Workbench with an **Assess** stage after **Propose**. It compares a feature proposal with the app’s current behavior before planning starts. Type `/`, select `/create-canvas`, and submit a focused change request that keeps the current canvas. Pick one small, beginner-safe improvement in `samples/book-app-web`, run the workbench through assess, plan, baseline, implement, and validate, and confirm that each completed stage has evidence from the current session.

pages.title: What’s next
pages.caption: In Chapter 07, you’ll turn repeatable prompts into automations. You’ll create a manual pull request readiness report and then schedule it. You don’t need to merge this chapter’s feature or keep its canvas open to continue.

pages.title: Awesome GitHub Copilot
pages.caption: A curated collection of agents, instructions, skills, and canvas extensions that you can install into the GitHub Copilot app. Enterprise-managed settings can restrict which plugins and marketplaces are available. If you cannot install the plugin, read Exercise 1 and continue to Exercise 2.

pages.title: Where canvas files live
pages.caption: `~/.copilot/extensions` is user scope: personal experiments, and the course’s choice, so nothing is committed. `.github/extensions` is project or team scope, for shared workflows. A canvas includes an entry file such as `extension.mjs`. Pause before accepting extra generated code: inspect capability names, stored state, UI controls, and whether any private data is included.

pages.title: The Markdown fallback
pages.caption: If `/create-canvas` is unavailable, or the generated canvas still does not work after two focused repairs, keep the same workflow in a Markdown artifact named `feature-workbench.md`, not added to the repository. Open it from the session’s **Files** tab. It has no action buttons, but it keeps the same plan and validation record visible. Update an item only after the session produces matching terminal, diff, or browser evidence.

pages.title: No canvas opens?
pages.caption: Confirm that you typed `/create-canvas`. Submit the prompt `Restart canvas extensions` once. If the command or the panel is still missing, use the Markdown fallback.

pages.title: The plan status stays at Working?
pages.caption: Answer the **Review plan** box at the bottom of the chat. Then select **Refresh evidence** on the canvas.

pages.title: An action button stays disabled?
pages.caption: The canvas enables each action only after the previous step has evidence. If **Implement** or **Run final checks** stays disabled because a screenshot or browser check could not run, use the **An action stays disabled** repair prompt in Exercise 3.

pages.title: The board does not match the evidence?
pages.caption: Compare the board with the terminal and browser output from this session’s worktree, not with an example image or another session. Confirm that commands ran in `samples/book-app-web`. Uncheck any item that has no output to support it, then run the check again.

glossary.definition: A shared board in the side panel that you and the agent can both see and update. Create one with `/create-canvas` and a description of the board you want, or install one through a plugin.
An action that the canvas gives the agent, such as updating a checklist item. On the Feature Workbench, each canvas button also asks the agent to do work, such as running tests.
The canvas is available to you across projects and is not committed to this repository.
The app’s test totals and build result before any change. The Feature Workbench records them first, and compares the final totals with them.
